# AccessBuddy Incident Report — Email Cap, Login Failure, Fob-Expiry Template

**Date:** 2026-08-01 · **Status:** DRAFT for Nick's review — no changes executed, nothing sent
**Sources:** three read-only Fable investigation agents (login flow, email pipeline audit, template forensics), file:line evidence throughout. Counts requiring prod DB access are marked UNKNOWN with the exact query to obtain them.

---

## Executive summary

The three reported issues are one incident with one root cause and one independent trigger.

On 1–2 August the 2am daily cron (`accessbuddy-daily-cron` → `/api/cron/daily`) sent 30-day fob-expiry warnings to the SMLSC seasonal cohort. Because the platform normalises season expiry to **1 September**, the entire active cohort (up to 354 credentials) qualified in a single run — far past Resend's free-tier cap of **100 emails/day**. Every send past the cap failed. The failure is swallowed in code (`sendEmail` logs, writes an `email_failed` audit row, returns void), so:

- **Issue 1 (login):** login is email-only (Firebase magic link in browser, 6-digit OTP in PWA). With the cap exhausted, auth emails fail silently while the UI says "we sent you a code". Members were logged out in the first place by the 14 July v1.11.0 deploy (`cd70131` rotated the session-signing key, invalidating all OTP/passkey sessions) and/or natural 14-day cookie expiry ~28 July. Logout was benign; the inability to log back in is the Resend cap.
- **Issue 2 (email limit):** sends past ~100/day failed silently; failed 30-day warnings are **permanently lost** (the warning fires only at exactly 30 days out; no dedupe/backfill). Two more cap-breaching spikes are already scheduled: **~25 Aug** (7-day warnings, same cohort) and **~1–2 Sep** (credential-expired blast).
- **Issue 3 (template):** the bare wording is the hardcoded code default — the per-tenant override system is dead configuration (the `email_configurations` table doesn't exist in prod; no send path reads it anyway). The cron also does **not** exclude members who already renewed (only fully reprogrammed-and-confirmed credentials are excluded), so renewed members legitimately got the warning — hence the confusion.

## Causal chain

```
Season expiry normalised to 1 Sep (route.ts:150)
  → whole cohort hits diffDays === 30 on the same day (1–2 Aug)
    → cron attempts up to ~354 sends in one run
      → Resend free tier caps at 100/day
        → sends 101+ fail; sendEmail swallows error (email.ts:224-249)
          → auth emails (magic link / OTP) also fail silently
            → members logged out by 14 Jul key rotation / cookie expiry cannot re-authenticate
```

Contributing factors: fire-and-forget send path (no queue, no retry, no daily budget); auth and bulk email share one unprioritised quota; template lacked business context since v1.0.0 (`f36375a`); override system unwired; no alerting on `email_failed` bursts.

---

## Issue 1 — Member cannot log in

**Root cause:** logout = session-signing key rotation (14 Jul deploy) or 14-day cookie expiry; blocked re-login = Resend cap + silently swallowed send failure (`email.ts:224-249` returns void; `/api/auth/send-otp` and `/api/auth/send-magic-link` return `{ sent: true }` regardless).

**Evidence:** `apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:9,59-93` (fail-closed HMAC verification, 14-day TTL); `sign-in-form.tsx:75-97` (email-only paths); commit `cd70131`; agents' full traces.

**Plan (in order):**
1. Check the Resend dashboard for quota state; daily reset is midnight UTC = 10:00 AEST.
2. Unblock the member today: passkey login if previously enrolled; otherwise resend OTP/magic link after quota reset; fallback — generate a Firebase sign-in link via Admin SDK and send it from your own mailbox (needs your approval to contact the member).
3. Pause or gate the cron's email sections until the queue/limit fix ships, so tomorrow's run doesn't re-break login.
4. Code fix (with issue 2): propagate send failures for auth-critical templates so sign-in routes return an honest error instead of `{ sent: true }`.
5. Comms: brief reply to the member (and any others who report it) explaining the outage window.

**Verification:** member confirms login; `audit_log` shows no `email_failed` rows for `verificationCode`/`magicLink` after fix.

## Issue 2 — Email cap: what sent, what didn't, and the queue

**What sent vs what didn't:** recoverable but UNKNOWN from this box — prod Cloud SQL is private-IP only, `gcloud` is not installed (Linux box or Mac), and both Resend API keys are send-only restricted (401 on read endpoints). Two paths to the numbers:
- **Fastest:** Resend dashboard → Emails view (or create a temporary full-access API key and `GET /emails`).
- **Authoritative:** one read-only psql session via cloud-sql-proxy; queries prepared (per-template sent/failed counts, failed-recipient list with error text, cohort-sizing by expiry day) — see Appendix A.

**Failure mode:** fire-and-forget; no retry, no queue; cron returns 200 even if every email failed; failed 30-day warnings never re-fire.

**Queue design (proposed):**
- New `email_queue` table (id, tenant, template, recipient, payload, priority, status, attempts, earliest_send_at, created_at, sent_at, error).
- **Priority classes:** P0 auth (magic link, OTP — sent inline, never queued, but counted); P1 transactional (payment, pickup, approval); P2 bulk (expiry warnings, summaries, correction blasts).
- **Daily budget:** cap outbound at **85/day** (100 − 15 reserved for P0 auth). A counter (Postgres, day-keyed) increments on every send including auth; the drain job stops P1/P2 when the counter hits 85, P0 always allowed to 100.
- **Drain:** cron (reuse `/api/cron/daily` or a new 15-min cron) drains queue oldest-first within priority, spreading the ~354-recipient cohort across ~4–5 days automatically.
- **Retry/backlog:** failed sends set `status='failed'` and re-queue with backoff (max 3 attempts); the currently-lost 30-day warnings get backfilled by enqueueing everyone from the failed-recipient query.
- **Cron change:** expiry-warning windows become ranges (e.g. 30–26 days and 7–3 days with sent-dedupe against `email_queue`/audit) so spreading over days doesn't skip anyone.
- **Guardrail:** alert (or at minimum a daily-summary line) when `email_failed` > 0 or queue depth > budget × 2.

**Alternative/complement:** Resend Pro (~US$20/mo, 50k emails/mo, no daily cap) removes the ceiling instantly. **Recommendation: do both** — upgrade now for the September crunch (renewal season traffic: warnings, expired notices, correction email, plus login traffic from confused members all collide this month), keep the queue as structural protection and for per-tenant budgets when tenant 2 lands.

**Verification:** cohort-sizing query shows no single day exceeding budget; simulated 429 produces queued retry, not silent loss.

## Issue 3 — Fob-expiry template + one-off correction

**What actually went out** (hardcoded default, certain — override system unwired and its table absent in prod):
> Subject: "ACTION REQUIRED: Your credential is expiring soon"
> "Dear \<First\>, Your credential expires on \<date\>. Please take action to renew it before it expires. Serial… Expires… Submit a renewal request through AccessBuddy to maintain your access."

The expiry date was present; the membership context was not, and it's been that way since v1.0.0. Renewed-but-not-yet-reprogrammed members were **not** excluded (only confirm-programming completion moves live `expiresAt`), so they received it too.

**Fix path:** edit the code default — `credentialExpiryWarningEmail()` in `apps/web/src/lib/email-templates.ts:614-636` and the subject at `email.ts:634`. Ship as `fix:` (release-please deploys `fix:`, not `chore:`). An override row is impossible (table missing) and would be inert anyway. Bundle in the same commit: skip warnings where `pendingExpiresAt` is set (renewal in pipeline), and give `credentialExpiredEmail()` the same context treatment before its 1 Sep firing.

**Corrected template copy (draft):**
> **Subject:** Your {club} fob will expire on {date} unless you renew your membership
>
> Hi {firstName},
>
> Your fob (serial {serial}) is due to expire on **{date}**.
>
> Fob access is tied to your club membership. If you renew your membership for the coming season, your fob stays active — its expiry is extended automatically once your renewal is processed, and you do not need to do anything with the fob itself.
>
> **If you have already renewed your membership, you can ignore this email.** Your fob's expiry will be updated shortly.
>
> If you have not renewed yet, please renew your membership before {date} to keep your access.
>
> Any questions, just reply to this email.

**One-off correction email (draft, to recipients of the bare email):**
> **Subject:** About the fob expiry email — what it actually means
>
> Hi {firstName},
>
> In the last few days you received an automated email from AccessBuddy saying your fob is expiring soon. Sorry — it was missing the context, and understandably caused some confusion.
>
> Here is the full picture: your fob will expire on **1 September** only if your club membership has not been renewed for the new season. Renewing your membership keeps your fob active — once your renewal is processed, the fob's expiry is extended automatically and you do not need to do anything with the fob itself.
>
> **If you have already renewed your membership, there is nothing you need to do** — please ignore both this and the earlier email.
>
> If you have not renewed yet, please renew before 1 September to keep your access.
>
> Apologies again for the confusion. The wording of the automated email has been fixed so future reminders explain this properly.

**Send plan for the correction:** recipient list from the audit-log query (Appendix A) — the successful `credentialExpiryWarning` sends of the last 4 days; send as P2 through the new queue (or manually throttled under the daily budget after the Resend upgrade); once-off script, not a new scheduled job; every send audited with subject per email standards.

**Verification:** rendered template screenshot with SMLSC branding before deploy; correction recipient list reviewed by you before send.

## Recommended execution order (on your approval)

1. **Today:** Resend dashboard — confirm quota state + failed sends; **upgrade to Pro** (removes the ceiling before the ~25 Aug and 1 Sep spikes). Unblock the locked-out member.
2. **Today/tomorrow:** pause cron email sections OR ship the template fix + `pendingExpiresAt` skip + auth-error propagation as one `fix:` release.
